transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is I keep messing up basic adult stuff. Like paying bills on time, replying to interview emails, showing up to appointments, finishing errands I said I’d do.

And it’s not like I don’t care, it’s just… I’ll think, “I’ll do that in a minute,” and then somehow it’s three days later. Or I remember at the worst possible time, like when I’m in the shower or trying to sleep. I had this whole thing where I was going to be really organized after graduation—I bought a planner and everything, it was cute, actually—but then I just stopped using it.

It’s started costing me real opportunities, especially with interviews and appointments, and I feel embarrassed because it sounds so simple when I say it out loud.
Thinking back, did you notice similar struggles with organization, forgetfulness, or follow-through when you were a kid or in school, or does this feel like something that started more recently?

No, it was definitely there when I was a kid. Like, elementary school report cards would say I was “bright” or “had potential,” which my mom loved to point out, but then right under it the teacher would be like, she loses worksheets, doesn’t follow directions carefully, talks out of turn.

My desk was a disaster too. Like those little lift-top desks? Mine was just… crumpled papers and broken pencils and random stuff, and I’d swear I did the assignment but then I couldn’t find it. I remember one time finding old worksheets weeks later, which is kind of funny now, but at the time I felt so stupid because everyone else just seemed to know where their things were. So yeah, not new. It’s just harder to hide now.
Do you also notice things like feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still, or often interrupting others or blurting things out?

Yeah, definitely the restless part. Like if I have to sit through an interview or a meeting, or even a movie—which is annoying because I like movies—I get this pressure inside my body, like I need to get up or shift around or do something with my hands.

It’s not even that the thing is bad, necessarily. I’ll be sitting there trying to look normal, and meanwhile I’m like, okay, don’t bounce your leg, don’t mess with your sleeve, don’t check your phone, just sit still. But it feels like I’m going to crawl out of my skin if I can’t move somehow.
Do you notice this restlessness and trouble focusing even when you're not feeling worried or anxious about anything in particular, like during a relaxed moment?

Yeah, I mean… it happens even when I’m not upset. Like, a movie is probably the best example, because I’m choosing to watch it, I’m relaxed, I have snacks or whatever, and still I get this feeling like I need to shift around or get up or keep my hands busy.

It’s like this pressure in my body, not always worry exactly. Sometimes I’ll be totally fine emotionally, but if I’m sitting too long—like in a meeting, or an interview, or even just watching something—I start feeling like I’m going to crawl out of my skin if I don’t move.
